clue.text: Imaginary god detailed in plan

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened god goes inside the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area

indicators.note: detailed read as de-tailed: the word for god loses its final letter

parts.note: deus is Latin for god

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a plan featuring an invented deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, losing its final letter, rather than as thorough; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made-up is invented, so imaginary in the sense of not real.

clue.text: Mention "A Taste of Bangkok" (Mansfield) to confuse

indicators.note: to mention something is to say it, so the phrase is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: a taste of Bangkok is a Thai meal, and Mansfield is a town in Notts (Nottinghamshire): a Thai in Notts

explanation.surface: It reads like a Thai restaurant in Mansfield given a show title, meant to baffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mansfield is a town in Nottinghamshire, abbreviated Notts; 'A Thai in Notts', said out loud, sounds like the idiom for bewildering someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone in knots is an idiom for muddling or bewildering them.

clue.text: Some 1,000,000€ I sense providing anxiety

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is kept, a run tucked inside them

parts.note: the figure is read out in words as million euros, followed by I sense

explanation.surface: Someone senses that having a million euros brings worry.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a hidden word once the sum is written out as 'million euros': milliON EUROS I Sense; the parse is written as dropping the letters on either side because the figure has no printed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by persistent worry, so a form of anxiety.

clue.text: Music player giving flower to bird

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Dee
the jay is a crow-family bird

explanation.surface: A DJ hands a flower to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword convention for a river (it flows); the Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: A deejay is a disc jockey, someone who plays recorded music for an audience.

clue.text: On which rep stood to be abused, or posted letters?

definitions.text: On which rep stood to be abused, or posted letters?

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so these letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sales rep stood on the step being shouted at, where letters also get delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a doorstep is where a door-to-door salesman stands, and where post arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The doorstep is the step outside a front door, where callers wait and mail is delivered.

clue.text: Sickening traveller Moore in "Odyssey", perhaps

indicators.note: in places the actress inside the poem type

parts.note: Homer's Odyssey is an example of an epic poem
Demi Moore is an American actress

explanation.surface: An ailing traveller appears in a film of the Odyssey starring Demi Moore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sickening traveller' looks like a person, but it is a disease that spreads from place to place.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is an outbreak of illness that travels through a population, making people sick.

clue.text: Job for metal worker, fascinating

definitions.meaning: fastening metal plates together with rivets is a metalworker's task
gripping or enthralling, holding one's attention

explanation.definitionFit: Riveting is both the act of fixing with rivets and, figuratively, holding attention fast.

clue.text: Time for someone stabbed in the back to accept end of tenure!

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the end letter goes inside

parts.note: IDS is Iain Duncan Smith, the Conservative leader ousted by his own party in 2003

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of tenure

explanation.surface: A politician betrayed by colleagues finally has to accept his time in office is up.
explanation.walkthrough: IDS are the initials of Iain Duncan Smith, a British Conservative leader removed by his own MPs; the surface also recalls Caesar, stabbed on the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides is a day in the Roman calendar, the mid-month date such as 15 March.

clue.text: Sound opening pace

indicators.note: sound here means said out loud, so a word heard is entered as its twin

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A sound start sets a good pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as healthy, but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gait is a manner of walking, a person's stride or pace.

clue.text: Musical piece for clarinet was finished by having one bar too many?

definitions.text: was finished by having one bar too many?

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical based on Oliver Twist
a reed is the vibrating part of a clarinet mouthpiece

explanation.surface: A clarinet part ends with an extra bar, as if overwritten.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor Oliver Reed died in 1999 after a heavy drinking session in a bar in Malta; the musical 'bar' in the surface becomes a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The English actor famously died after a drinking bout in a pub, the cryptic picture here.

clue.text: Guide's statement reversed about one's king and prime minister

indicators.note: about means going round, so the backwards words surround the next pieces
reversed means the guide's words are read backwards

parts.note: a guide would say I lead
one is I, and one's gives I'S
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A tour guide's remarks are turned round to concern a king and a premier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns I LEAD into DAELI; 'about' puts IS plus R inside it after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice British Prime Minister under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Collective ventures which Corbett had a hand in, those rarely done, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the words are heard, not read, giving a sound-alike

parts.words: which Corbett had a hand in, those rarely done
parts.note: Harry Corbett's glove puppet was Sweep, which he had his hand in; things often done rare are steaks

explanation.surface: Joint enterprises that the TV entertainer Corbett was involved in.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweep was a puppet dog on British children's TV, worked by Harry Corbett's hand; SWEEPS plus STEAKS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery where everyone stakes money into a shared pot, a collective gamble.

clue.text: One's shaken given leak from ANC's 9?

parts.note: the answer to 9 is OLIVER, and Oliver Tambo was president of the ANC
to have a leak is slang for to urinate

explanation.surface: A political figure has to take a leak, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 9-across gives Oliver, so 'ANC's 9' is Oliver Tambo of South Africa's ANC; 'leak' is British slang for urination.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a percussion instrument played by shaking it so its jingles rattle.

clue.text: Departures from here, where arrivals expect to be late if leader changes

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for another one

parts.words: where arrivals expect to be late
parts.note: late means dead, and new arrivals on death row expect execution

explanation.surface: Passengers at an airport expect delays when the boss is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means deceased, not delayed; swap the D of DEATH ROW for H.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's main airport, where many flights depart.

clue.text: Unseat figure after the road swiftly bends

indicators.note: after puts the number behind the rearranged letters
the letters take sharp bends, rearranging themselves

parts.note: taken as written
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A rider is thrown off when the road suddenly curves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swiftly bends' is the anagram signal on 'the road' (with road abbreviated), and 'after' puts the figure behind it; the surface pictures a rider thrown on a sharp bend.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone is to remove a ruler from power, to unseat them.

clue.text: Drug given to farmyard animals merits witty remark

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy
a pig is a farmyard animal
a ram is another farmyard animal

explanation.surface: Feeding drugs to livestock deserves a quip.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two animals, PIG and RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, clever saying, a pithy witticism.

clue.text: Mineral lacks torrent?

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the preceding letters are ripped up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the first three letters of torrent

explanation.surface: A mineral lacking a rushing stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torrent' must be split into two parts: its first three letters join 'lacks' as fodder, and its last four, 'rent' (torn), are the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salt is halite, natural sodium chloride found as a crystalline mineral.

clue.text: Rude boy nearly sent back for tantrum

indicators.note: sent back means turned round, read in reverse
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as a synonym for itself
to make a scene is to throw a tantrum

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered lad is nearly sent home for a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims BOY to BO and 'sent back' turns it to OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensively indecent, so crude or rude.

clue.text: Upset at pain from running: this isn't running

parts.note: cross means annoyed or upset
a stitch is a sharp side pain from running

explanation.surface: A jogger is annoyed at getting a stitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A running stitch is a simple sewing stitch; the clue says the answer is a different kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-stitch is a sewing stitch distinct from running stitch, the cryptic contrast here.

clue.text: Local clergyman turns up in brown

indicators.note: in places the reversed clergyman within the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: turns up means read upwards in this down entry, so reversed

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A local vicar shows up dressed in brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and a tavern is an inn or pub.

clue.text: See 9
Sort of escape from sack

definitions.meaning: a type of escape route from a burning building
to sack is to dismiss from a job

explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is an emergency exit, and to fire someone is to dismiss them.

clue.text: Representative of ruler receiving backing of fool by day's end

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last letter follows
receiving means taking in, so the ruler encloses the reversed fool

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler

indicators.note: backing means reversing, so the fool is read backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: end picks out the last letter of day

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A ruler's envoy takes in a backward fool at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' signals the reversal of the fool, 'receiving' puts it inside the ruler, and 'end' takes the final letter of 'day', ignoring the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent as a representative on a mission.

clue.text: Exaggerate when scorer lacks finish in goalless draw

indicators.note: in places the shortened composer between the two zeros

parts.note: a nil-nil score is written 0-0, read as OO

indicators.note: lacks finish means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a scorer is a composer of musical scores, here Verdi

explanation.surface: A football pundit overstates things when the striker can't finish in a 0-0 game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a footballer but means a composer of scores; 'lacks finish' drops his last letter, and a 0-0 draw supplies two Os around him.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it too far, to exaggerate.

clue.text: House plant turning blue first

indicators.note: first puts the turned word in front of the plant
turning means the word is turned around

parts.note: blue can mean risqué or lewd
ling is heather, a plant

explanation.surface: A houseplant goes blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House plant' reads as one thing; 'House' is the definition, and 'blue' means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house, a place where people live.

clue.text: What cows do, causing altercation amid what they had

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the quarrel sits inside

parts.note: BSE, mad cow disease, is what British cattle had in the 1990s
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Grazing cattle squabble in the middle of their disease crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, the 1990s UK mad cow epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to graze on leaves and shoots, as cattle feed.
